q: A company hosts a multiplayer gaming application on AWS. The company wants the application to read data with sub-millisecond latency and run one-time queries on historical data. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.t: Store the data directly in an Amazon S3 bucket. Implement an S3 Lifecycle policy to move older data to S3 Glacier Deep Archive for longterm storage. Run one-time queries on the data in Amazon S3 by using Amazon Athena.
o.w: Storing the live data directly in S3 does not provide sub-millisecond read latency; S3 is an object store optimized for durability and throughput, not the ultra-low-latency access pattern described for gameplay data.

o.t: Use Amazon RDS for data that is frequently accessed. Run a periodic custom script to export the data to an Amazon S3 bucket.
o.w: Amazon RDS (a relational database) does not natively provide sub-millisecond read latency on its own, and this option lacks any dedicated caching layer while also requiring a custom export script, adding operational overhead.

o.t: Use Amazon DynamoDB for data that is frequently accessed. Turn on streaming to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to read the data from Kinesis Data Streams. Store the records in an Amazon S3 bucket.
o.w: Streaming frequently accessed data through Kinesis Data Streams and Firehose into S3 is a reasonable export pipeline, but DynamoDB alone (without DAX) does not guarantee sub-millisecond read latency for the live, frequently accessed gameplay data path.

o.t: Use Amazon DynamoDB with DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) for data that is frequently accessed. Export the data to an Amazon S3 bucket by using DynamoDB table export. Run one-time queries on the data in Amazon S3 by using Amazon Athena.
o.w: DynamoDB with DAX provides the sub-millisecond read latency needed for live gameplay data, and periodically exporting historical data to S3 via DynamoDB table export lets Athena run one-time queries on the historical data cheaply — all with managed services and the least operational overhead.

explain:
Amazon DynamoDB with DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX):

DynamoDB is a highly scalable and low-latency NoSQL database, suitable for frequently accessed data.
DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is a caching layer that provides sub-millisecond read latencies for DynamoDB.
Export Data to Amazon S3:

Use DynamoDB table export to periodically export historical data to an Amazon S3 bucket.
This allows you to store historical data in a cost-effective manner while still benefiting from DynamoDB for frequently accessed data.
Amazon Athena for One-time Queries:

Amazon Athena allows you to run SQL queries directly on data stored in Amazon S3.
By using Athena, you can perform one-time queries on the historical data without the need to manage a separate database.

q: A company is launching a new application and will display application metrics on an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard. The company's product manager needs to access this dashboard periodically. The product manager does not have an AWS account. A solutions architect must provide access to the product manager by following the principle of least privilege. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.t: Create an IAM user for the company's employees. Attach the ViewOnlyAccess AWS managed policy to the IAM user. Share the new login credentials with the product manager. Ask the product manager to navigate to the CloudWatch console and locate the dashboard by name in the Dashboards section.
o.w: Creating a full IAM user with console access and attaching the broad ViewOnlyAccess managed policy grants far more permissions (read access to most AWS services) than the product manager needs just to view one dashboard, violating least privilege.

o.t: Share the dashboard from the CloudWatch console. Enter the product manager's email address, and complete the sharing steps. Provide a shareable link for the dashboard to the product manager.
o.w: The native CloudWatch dashboard sharing feature lets you share a specific dashboard via an email-verified link without creating any IAM identity at all, matching exactly the least-privilege need of letting the product manager view just that one dashboard with no AWS account.

o.t: Create an IAM user specifically for the product manager. Attach the CloudWatchReadOnlyAccess AWS managed policy to the user. Share the new login credentials with the product manager. Share the browser URL of the correct dashboard with the product manager.
o.w: Creating a dedicated IAM user with the CloudWatchReadOnlyAccess policy still grants read access across all CloudWatch resources and dashboards, which is broader than the single dashboard needed, and it requires issuing and managing login credentials for an external user.

o.t: Deploy a bastion server in a public subnet. When the product manager requires access to the dashboard, start the server and share the RDP credentials. On the bastion server, ensure that the browser is configured to open the dashboard URL with cached AWS credentials that have appropriate permissions to view the dashboard.
o.w: Standing up a bastion server with RDP access and cached broad AWS credentials is a far more complex, higher-privilege, and higher-operational-effort approach than simply using CloudWatch's built-in dashboard sharing link.

explain: Share a single dashboard and designate specific email addresses of the people who can view the dashboard. Each of these users creates their own password that they must enter to view the dashboard.

q: A company has an application that ingests incoming messages. Dozens of other applications and microservices then quickly consume these messages. The number of messages varies drastically and sometimes increases suddenly to 100,000 each second. The company wants to decouple the solution and increase scalability. Which solution meets these requirements?

o.t: Deploy the ingestion application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group to scale the number of EC2 instances based on CPU metrics.
o.w: Scaling the ingestion application's EC2 instances based on CPU metrics doesn't decouple message ingestion from downstream consumers, so a sudden burst to 100,000 messages per second could still overwhelm the consuming applications without a buffering layer.

o.t: Publish the messages to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic with multiple Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SOS) subscriptions. Configure the consumer applications to process the messages from the queues.
o.w: Publishing to an SNS topic with multiple SQS subscriptions is the standard fan-out pattern: SNS lets dozens of decoupled consumer applications each receive messages through their own durable SQS queue, absorbing huge bursts and letting each consumer process independently at its own pace.

o.t: Write the messages to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with a single shard. Use an AWS Lambda function to preprocess messages and store them in Amazon DynamoDB. Configure the consumer applications to read from DynamoDB to process the messages.
o.w: A single-shard Kinesis stream has a hard throughput ceiling (roughly 1,000 records per second per shard), which would throttle well below a 100,000-message-per-second spike, and it does not naturally fan out to dozens of independent consumer applications the way SNS/SQS does.

o.t: Persist the messages to Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics. Configure the consumer applications to read and process the messages.
o.w: Kinesis Data Analytics is built for running SQL/streaming analytics over a data stream; it is not a general-purpose message ingestion and fan-out mechanism for dozens of independent consumer applications.

explain:
A good practice is to also add message attributes when publishing to SNS. Each SQS subscription can have a filter policy that matches only the messages it cares about, so that only relevant messages are delivered to each SQS queue, and consumers only see/process what they need.

an SQS queue can handle a maximum of 3,000 messages per second. However, you can request higher throughput by contacting AWS Support. AWS can increase the message throughput for your queue beyond the default limits in increments of 300 messages per second, up to a maximum of 10,000 messages per second.

It's important to note that the maximum number of messages per second that a queue can handle is not the same as the maximum number of requests per second that the SQS API can handle. The SQS API is designed to handle a high volume of requests per second, so it can be used to send messages to your queue at a rate that exceeds the maximum message throughput of the queue.

q: A company’s application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. On the first day of every month at midnight, the application becomes much slower when the month-end financial calculation batch runs. This causes the CPU utilization of the EC2 instances to immediately peak to 100%, which disrupts the application. What should a solutions architect recommend to ensure the application is able to handle the workload and avoid downtime?

o.t: Configure Amazon ElastiCache to remove some of the workload from the EC2 instances.
o.w: ElastiCache helps offload repeated read queries from a database; it has no effect on a compute-bound CPU spike caused by a backend financial calculation batch job.

o.t: Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the ALB.
o.w: CloudFront is a content-delivery cache for static or cacheable content; it does nothing to reduce the compute load generated by a backend batch processing job.

o.t: Configure an EC2 Auto Scaling simple scaling policy based on CPU utilization.
o.w: A simple scaling policy based on CPU reacts only after utilization has already spiked, which can be too late to prevent the instances from already hitting 100% CPU and disrupting the application for a known, recurring event.

o.t: Configure an EC2 Auto Scaling scheduled scaling policy based on the monthly schedule.
o.w: A scheduled scaling policy can proactively add capacity ahead of the known, recurring first-of-month timing, before CPU utilization spikes, preventing disruption for this predictable monthly event.

explain:
By configuring a scheduled scaling policy, the EC2 Auto Scaling group can proactively launch additional EC2 instances before the CPU utilization peaks to 100%. This will ensure that the application can handle the workload during the month-end financial calculation batch, and avoid any disruption or downtime.

Configuring a simple scaling policy based on CPU utilization or adding Amazon CloudFront distribution or Amazon ElastiCache will not directly address the issue of handling the monthly peak workload.

q: A company has applications hosted on Amazon EC2 instances with IPv6 addresses. The applications must initiate communications with other external applications using the internet. However the company’s security policy states that any external service cannot initiate a connection to the EC2 instances. What should a solutions architect recommend to resolve this issue?

o.t: Create an egress-only internet gateway and make it the destination of the subnet's route table
o.w: An egress-only internet gateway is purpose-built for IPv6 traffic, allowing outbound connections initiated by resources inside the VPC while blocking any inbound connection initiated from the internet — exactly matching the requirement.

o.t: Create a virtual private gateway and make it the destination of the subnet's route table
o.w: A virtual private gateway is used for VPN or Direct Connect connectivity to on-premises networks; it does not control general internet-bound IPv6 traffic for EC2 instances.

o.t: Create a NAT gateway and make it the destination of the subnet's route table
o.w: A NAT gateway is designed for IPv4 traffic from instances without public IPv4 addresses; it does not support or apply to IPv6 traffic at all.

o.t: Create an internet gateway and make it the destination of the subnet's route table
o.w: A standard internet gateway allows bidirectional traffic, meaning external services could initiate inbound connections to the instances, which directly violates the requirement that no external service can initiate a connection.

explain:
An egress-only internet gateway is used for IPv6 traffic leaving the VPC to reach the internet. It allows outbound communication initiated by resources inside the VPC but prevents incoming traffic initiated from the internet.
Configuring the subnet's route table to use the egress-only internet gateway as the destination ensures that IPv6 traffic initiated from EC2 instances can reach external services while blocking unsolicited incoming traffic.

q: A company has thousands of edge devices that collectively generate 1 TB of status alerts each day. Each alert is approximately 2 KB in size. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution to ingest and store the alerts for future analysis. The company wants a highly available solution. However, the company needs to minimize costs and does not want to manage additional infrastructure. Additionally, the company wants to keep 14 days of data available for immediate analysis and archive any data older than 14 days. What is the MOST operationally efficient solution that meets these requirements?

o.t: Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to ingest the alerts. Configure the Kinesis Data Firehose stream to deliver the alerts to an Amazon S3 bucket. Set up an S3 Lifecycle configuration to transition data to Amazon S3 Glacier after 14 days.
o.w: Kinesis Data Firehose is a fully managed, serverless ingestion service that requires no infrastructure to manage, delivering alerts directly to S3, and an S3 Lifecycle rule automatically transitions data older than 14 days to Glacier — meeting availability, cost, no-infrastructure, and retention requirements with minimal operational effort.

o.t: Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to ingest the alerts. Configure the Kinesis Data Firehose stream to deliver the alerts to an Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service) cluster. Set up the Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service) cluster to take manual snapshots every day and delete data from the cluster that is older than 14 days.
o.w: Delivering into an OpenSearch Service cluster requires provisioning and managing cluster capacity (which is infrastructure the company explicitly doesn't want to manage), plus manually scripting daily snapshots and deletions, adding significant operational overhead.

o.t: Launch Amazon EC2 instances across two Availability Zones and place them behind an Elastic Load Balancer to ingest the alerts. Create a script on the EC2 instances that will store the alerts in an Amazon S3 bucket. Set up an S3 Lifecycle configuration to transition data to Amazon S3 Glacier after 14 days.
o.w: Launching and load-balancing EC2 instances to ingest alerts requires the company to provision, patch, and manage its own servers and custom ingestion scripts, directly conflicting with the requirement to avoid managing additional infrastructure.

o.t: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queue to ingest the alerts, and set the message retention period to 14 days. Configure consumers to poll the SQS queue, check the age of the message, and analyze the message data as needed. If the message is 14 days old, the consumer should copy the message to an Amazon S3 bucket and delete the message from the SQS queue.
o.w: Using SQS with consumers that poll, check message age, and manually copy old messages to S3 requires building and maintaining custom application logic, which is far less operationally efficient than a managed Firehose delivery stream with a native S3 Lifecycle policy.

explain: Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose is a fully managed service that can capture, transform, and deliver streaming data into storage systems or analytics tools, making it an ideal solution for ingesting and storing status alerts. In this solution, the Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream ingests the alerts and delivers them to an S3 bucket, which is a cost-effective storage solution. An S3 Lifecycle configuration is set up to transition the data to Amazon S3 Glacier after 14 days to minimize storage costs.

q: A company has one million users that use its mobile app. The company must analyze the data usage in near-real time. The company also must encrypt the data in near-real time and must store the data in a centralized location in Apache Parquet format for further processing. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.t: Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to store the data in Amazon S3. Create an Amazon EMR cluster to analyze the data.
o.w: Kinesis Data Firehose can deliver to S3, but adding an EMR cluster for near-real-time analysis means provisioning and managing cluster infrastructure, which is more operational overhead than using serverless Kinesis Data Analytics.

o.t: Create an Amazon Kinesis data stream to store the data in Amazon S3. Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics application to analyze the data. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to send the data to the Kinesis Data Analytics application.
o.w: A raw Kinesis data stream does not natively write to S3 or convert data to Parquet, and this option requires an extra Lambda function plus a separate Data Analytics application, adding more moving parts than a direct Firehose-based pipeline.

o.t: Create an Amazon Kinesis data stream to store the data in Amazon S3. Create an Amazon EMR cluster to analyze the data. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to send the data to the EMR cluster.
o.w: This option requires managing a Kinesis data stream, a custom Lambda function, and an EMR cluster together — considerably more operational overhead than a managed Firehose-plus-Data-Analytics pipeline.

o.t: Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to store the data in Amazon S3. Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics application to analyze the data.
o.w: Kinesis Data Firehose natively supports converting streaming data to Apache Parquet, encrypting it, and delivering it directly to S3, while a Kinesis Data Analytics application analyzes the stream in near real time — all fully managed, with the least operational overhead.

q: A company runs a critical, customer-facing application on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). The application has a microservices architecture. The company needs to implement a solution that collects, aggregates, and summarizes metrics and logs from the application in a centralized location. Which solution meets these requirements?

o.t: Run AWS App Mesh in the existing EKS cluster. View the metrics and logs in the App Mesh console.
o.w: AWS App Mesh is a service mesh for managing service-to-service traffic and communication; it is not a centralized metrics-and-logs aggregation and visualization tool.

o.t: Configure Amazon CloudWatch Container Insights in the existing EKS cluster. View the metrics and logs in the CloudWatch console.
o.w: CloudWatch Container Insights is purpose-built to collect, aggregate, and summarize metrics and logs from containerized applications running on EKS/ECS and present them centrally in the CloudWatch console, directly meeting the requirement.

o.t: Configure AWS CloudTrail to capture data events. Query CloudTrail by using Amazon OpenSearch Service.
o.w: AWS CloudTrail captures API call and data events for auditing purposes; it is not designed to collect application performance metrics and logs from microservices running on EKS.

o.t: Run the Amazon CloudWatch agent in the existing EKS cluster. View the metrics and logs in the CloudWatch console.
o.w: Simply running the standalone CloudWatch agent without enabling Container Insights does not provide the same automatic aggregation and summarization of Kubernetes- and container-specific metrics and logs that Container Insights delivers out of the box.

explain: CloudWatch Container Insights is specifically designed for monitoring containerized applications on Amazon EKS and ECS. It provides visibility into the performance of containers, clusters, and microservices.

q: A company has created a multi-tier application for its ecommerce website. The website uses an Application Load Balancer that resides in the public subnets, a web tier in the public subnets, and a MySQL cluster hosted on Amazon EC2 instances in the private subnets. The MySQL database needs to retrieve product catalog and pricing information that is hosted on the internet by a third-party provider. A solutions architect must devise a strategy that maximizes security without increasing operational overhead. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.t: Deploy a NAT gateway in the public subnets. Modify the private subnet route table to direct all internet-bound traffic to the NAT gateway.
o.w: A NAT gateway placed in a public subnet, with the private subnet's route table directing outbound traffic to it, lets the private MySQL instances initiate connections to the third-party pricing API without being directly exposed to inbound internet traffic, and it's a fully managed service requiring no patching.

o.t: Configure a virtual private gateway and attach it to the VPC. Modify the private subnet route table to direct internet-bound traffic to the virtual private gateway.
o.w: A virtual private gateway is used for VPN or Direct Connect connectivity to on-premises networks; it does not provide general internet access for instances in a private subnet.

o.t: Configure an internet gateway and attach it to the VPModify the private subnet route table to direct internet-bound traffic to the internet gateway.
o.w: Attaching an internet gateway and routing the private subnet's traffic through it would risk exposing the database instances to inbound internet reachability, undermining the goal of maximizing security for the private database tier.

o.t: Deploy a NAT instance in the VPC. Route all the internet-based traffic through the NAT instance.
o.w: A self-managed NAT instance requires the company to patch, scale, and maintain the instance itself, which increases operational overhead compared to the fully managed NAT gateway.

explain: A NAT gateway is a fully managed service provided by AWS that allows instances in a private subnet to initiate outbound traffic to the internet while preventing inbound traffic from reaching those instances. It simplifies the process of enabling internet access for instances in private subnets without the need for managing a separate NAT instance.

q: A company runs multiple Amazon EC2 Linux instances in a VPC across two Availability Zones. The instances host applications that use a hierarchical directory structure. The applications need to read and write rapidly and concurrently to shared storage. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.t: Create a file system on a Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Attach the EBS volume to all the EC2 instances.
o.w: EBS volumes can generally only be attached to one instance at a time for read/write (outside of specialized io2 Multi-Attach clustering, which still doesn't provide a shared general-purpose filesystem), so a normal EBS volume isn't suited for concurrent multi-instance read/write.

o.t: Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Allow access from all the EC2 instances in the VPC.
o.w: Amazon S3 is an object store, not a POSIX-compliant hierarchical filesystem, so it cannot support the hierarchical directory structure with fast concurrent file-level read/write access that the applications need.

o.t: Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system from each EC2 instance.
o.w: Amazon EFS provides a shared, POSIX-compliant, hierarchical file system that multiple EC2 instances across Availability Zones can mount and access concurrently, enabling the fast concurrent read/write access the applications require.

o.t: Create file systems on Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes that are attached to each EC2 instance. Synchronize the EBS volumes across the different EC2 instances.
o.w: Running separate EBS volumes per instance and trying to synchronize them is not a true shared filesystem and would introduce consistency lag and operational complexity, unlike a natively shared EFS file system.

explain: Amazon EFS is a fully managed, scalable file storage service designed to provide shared access to files across multiple Amazon EC2 instances. It is particularly well-suited for use cases that require concurrent access from multiple instances.

q: A development team has launched a new application that is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances inside a development VPC. A solutions architect needs to create a new VPC in the same account. The new VPC will be peered with the development VPC. The VPC CIDR block for the development VPC is 192.168.0.0/24. The solutions architect needs to create a CIDR block for the new VPC. The CIDR block must be valid for a VPC peering connection to the development VPC. What is the SMALLEST CIDR block that meets these requirements?

o.w: Spot Instances offer substantial discounts over On-Demand pricing, and since the batch jobs are fault-tolerant (another instance reprocesses a failed job), using Spot capacity with a CPU-based scaling policy meets the nightly workload most cost-effectively.

Staying on On-Demand pricing while just increasing instance size and scaling on CPU raises capacity but applies no pricing discount, so costs remain higher than necessary for this fault-tolerant batch workload.

A 1-year Reserved Instance commits to paying for a specific instance type and OS continuously for a year, even though the batch job only runs about 6 hours a night, wasting money on unused reserved capacity the rest of the day.

A 1-year Savings Plan likewise commits to a steady hourly spend regardless of the limited nightly usage window, which is less cost-effective than Spot pricing for this fault-tolerant, interruption-tolerant, short-duration nightly workload.

explain:
This is a valid CIDR block that does not overlap with the existing development VPC (192.168.0.0/24).

Therefore, this is the SMALLEST CIDR block that meets the requirements.

q: A company stores raw collected data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The data is used for several types of analytics on behalf of the company's customers. The type of analytics requested determines the access pattern on the S3 objects. The company cannot predict or control the access pattern. The company wants to reduce its S3 costs. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.t: Use S3 Lifecycle rules to transition objects from S3 Standard to Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA)
o.w: Referencing a security group ID as the source or destination automatically applies to every current and future instance associated with that security group, cleanly scoping access between tiers and supporting least privilege as the fleet changes over time.

o.t: Use S3 replication to transition infrequently accessed objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA)
o.w: Referencing individual instance IDs doesn't scale and doesn't automatically track Auto Scaling group membership — every time an instance is replaced, the rules would need to be manually updated, which isn't maintainable or truly least-privilege.

o.t: Use S3 Inventory to identify and transition objects that have not been accessed from S3 Standard to S3 Intelligent-Tiering
o.w: Using the entire VPC CIDR block as the source or destination would allow traffic from every resource in the VPC, not just the intended tier, which over-permits access and violates least privilege.

o.t: Use S3 Lifecycle rules to transition objects from S3 Standard to S3 Intelligent-Tiering
o.w: Using subnet CIDR blocks is broader than necessary if multiple unrelated resource types share a subnet, and it doesn't automatically adapt as instances change the way security-group-based rules do, making it a less precise least-privilege control.

explain:
S3 Intelligent-Tiering is designed to optimize costs by automatically moving objects between two access tiers: frequent and infrequent access. It is well-suited for scenarios where access patterns are unpredictable.
Using S3 Lifecycle rules to transition objects to S3 Intelligent-Tiering allows you to take advantage of automatic cost savings based on actual access patterns without the need for manual adjustments.

q: A company is moving its data management application to AWS. The company wants to transition to an event-driven architecture. The architecture needs to be more distributed and to use serverless concepts while performing the different aspects of the workflow. The company also wants to minimize operational overhead. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.t: Build out the workflow in Amazon EventBridge. Use EventBridge to invoke AWS Lambda functions on a schedule to process the workflow steps.
o.w: REST APIs in API Gateway support a private VPC Link, which lets API Gateway securely forward requests to backend services running in private subnets (like the ECS tasks) over a managed, private connection, matching both the REST interface and private backend requirements.

o.t: Build out the workflow in AWS Step Functions. Use Step Functions to create a state machine. Use the state machine to invoke AWS Lambda functions to process the workflow steps.
o.w: WebSocket APIs are built for persistent, bidirectional connections such as chat or real-time apps, not for the REST interface the company specifically requires for its search catalog frontend.

o.t: Build out the workflow in AWS Step Functions. Deploy the application on Amazon EC2 instances. Use Step Functions to invoke the workflow steps on the EC2 instances.
o.w: API Gateway resources don't attach to a security group the way an EC2 instance does; private connectivity from API Gateway into a VPC backend requires a VPC Link, not a security group association, so this option describes a mechanism that doesn't actually provide the needed private connection.

o.t: Build out the workflow in AWS Glue. Use AWS Glue to invoke AWS Lambda functions to process the workflow steps.
o.w: This combines the wrong API type (WebSocket instead of the required REST) even though a VPC Link is the correct private connectivity mechanism, so it still fails to meet the stated REST API requirement.

explain:
AWS Step Functions allows you to coordinate the components of distributed applications using visual workflows. It is a fully managed service, which means you don't need to worry about operational overhead.

State machines in AWS Step Functions enable you to define the workflow of your application by specifying a series of steps. Each step can invoke an AWS Lambda function, among other things.

AWS Lambda is a serverless compute service, and it automatically scales with the workload. This aligns with the goal of using serverless concepts and minimizing operational overhead.

q: A company is developing software that uses a PostgreSQL database schema. The company needs to configure multiple development environments and databases for the company's developers. On average, each development environment is used for half of the 8-hour workday. Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

o.t: Configure each development environment with its own Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database
o.w: A VPC customer-managed prefix list centralizes the office CIDR ranges, and AWS RAM lets that single prefix list be shared across the entire organization; security groups reference the prefix list, so updating CIDRs in one place propagates everywhere, minimizing administrative overhead cost-effectively.

o.t: Configure each development environment with its own Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Single-AZ DB instances
o.w: AWS Security Hub aggregates security findings and posture information; it is not an enforcement mechanism for pushing security group updates, and pairing it with a custom Lambda function to maintain a managed prefix list is more complex than simply sharing one customer-managed prefix list.

o.t: Configure each development environment with its own Amazon Aurora On-Demand PostgreSQL-Compatible database
o.w: AWS Firewall Manager with common security group policies is intended for broader organization-wide firewall and security policy enforcement, making it a heavier-handed and less cost-effective solution for the narrower, simpler need of propagating updated CIDR ranges.

o.t: Configure each development environment with its own Amazon S3 bucket by using Amazon S3 Object Select
o.w: Keeping security groups (even centrally defined) in the organization's management account still requires updating the same CIDR values across multiple accounts and Regions wherever those groups or their copies are used, which is exactly the administrative overhead the company wants to avoid.

explain: Explanation: Since each environment is only used for half of the workday, a standard RDS for PostgreSQL instance that gets stopped when not in use is cheaper than running Aurora continuously — Aurora costs more than standard RDS and this workload doesn't need Aurora's extra performance/availability features.

q: A company is using Amazon CloudFront with its website. The company has enabled logging on the CloudFront distribution, and logs are saved in one of the company’s Amazon S3 buckets. The company needs to perform advanced analyses on the logs and build visualizations. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

o.t: Use standard SQL queries in Amazon DynamoDB to analyze the CloudFront logs in the S3 bucket. Visualize the results with Amazon QuickSight.
o.w: Hosting all three tiers on EC2 preserves the ability to use native SQL Server backups and Data Quality Services (features not available on managed RDS), and Amazon FSx for Windows File Server provides fully SMB-compatible file sharing between the Windows-based tiers.

o.t: Use standard SQL queries in Amazon Athena to analyze the CloudFront logs in the S3 bucket. Visualize the results with Amazon QuickSight.
o.w: FSx File Gateway is meant to cache on-premises access to an existing Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system in the cloud; it is not intended as the direct file-sharing layer between EC2 application tiers that are already running in AWS.

o.t: Use standard SQL queries in Amazon Athena to analyze the CloudFront logs in the S3 bucket. Visualize the results with AWS Glue.
o.w: Amazon RDS does not support the specific SQL Server features mentioned, such as native backups and Data Quality Services, so hosting the database tier on RDS would prevent the company from using capabilities it explicitly wants to keep.

o.t: Use standard SQL queries in Amazon DynamoDB to analyze the CloudFront logs in the S3 bucket. Visualize the results with AWS Glue.
o.w: RDS again cannot support native backups or Data Quality Services, and a single EBS volume cannot be concurrently mounted and shared as a file system across multiple EC2 instances in different tiers.

explain:
Amazon Athena allows you to run standard SQL queries directly on the CloudFront logs stored in the S3 bucket. This enables you to perform advanced analyses on the log data.

Once you have queried and processed the CloudFront log data using Athena, you can use Amazon QuickSight for data visualization and building visualizations.

Amazon QuickSight is a business intelligence (BI) tool that allows you to create interactive dashboards and visualizations from various data sources, including the results of Athena queries.

q: A company previously migrated its data warehouse solution to AWS. The company also has an AWS Direct Connect connection. Corporate office users query the data warehouse using a visualization tool. The average size of a query returned by the data warehouse is 50 MB and each webpage sent by the visualization tool is approximately 500 KB. Result sets returned by the data warehouse are not cached. Which solution provides the LOWEST data transfer egress cost for the company?

o.t: Host the visualization tool in the same AWS Region as the data warehouse and access it over a Direct Connect connection at a location in the same Region.
o.w: Changing the instance class addresses raw compute/IO capacity but does not provide connection pooling, so bursty serverless clients can still exhaust the maximum connection limit and trigger rejection errors.

o.t: Host the visualization tool on premises and query the data warehouse directly over the internet.
o.w: ElastiCache is a caching layer for query results; it does not manage or pool database connections, so it would not resolve connection-rejection errors caused by too many concurrent serverless connections.

o.t: Host the visualization tool in the same AWS Region as the data warehouse. Access it over the internet.
o.w: Amazon RDS Proxy pools and shares database connections, allowing many serverless/Lambda clients to connect through the proxy rather than opening a new connection to the database each time, resolving connection exhaustion with minimal operational effort.

o.t: Host the visualization tool on premises and query the data warehouse directly over a Direct Connect connection at a location in the same AWS Region.
o.w: Multi-AZ provides a standby for failover and availability; it does not provide connection pooling or increase the number of concurrent connections the primary database can accept during traffic spikes.

explain: Hosting the visualization tool in the same AWS Region as the data warehouse and accessing it over a Direct Connect connection within the same Region minimizes data transfer costs. Since the data warehouse and the visualization tool are in the same Region, the data transfer between them doesn't incur the usual costs associated with data leaving the AWS network.

q: A solutions architect needs to review a company's Amazon S3 buckets to discover personally identifiable information (PII). The company stores the PII data in the us-east-1 Region and us-west-2 Region. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.t: Configure AWS Security Hub for all Regions. Create an AWS Config rule to analyze the data that is in Amazon S3.
o.w: Amazon Macie is a data discovery and classification service for finding sensitive data; it does not let the compliance team administer encryption keys used for data at rest.

o.t: Configure Amazon Inspector to analyze the data that is in Amazon S3.
o.w: SSE-S3 uses keys that are owned and fully managed by AWS; the compliance team has no ability to create, rotate, or otherwise administer these keys themselves.

o.t: Configure Amazon Macie in each Region. Create a job to analyze the data that is in Amazon S3.
o.w: The aws:SecureTransport condition enforces HTTPS/TLS-only connections for encryption in transit, and SSE-KMS with a customer managed key lets the compliance team directly administer the key policy and lifecycle for encryption at rest, satisfying both requirements.

o.t: Configure Amazon GuardDuty to analyze the data that is in Amazon S3.
o.w: Issuing a public TLS certificate through ACM and 'associating' it with S3 is not how S3 encrypts requests in transit (S3 already provides its own HTTPS endpoints), making this an unnecessary, non-functional extra step compared to simply relying on the SecureTransport condition.

explain: Amazon Macie is a managed data security and data privacy service that uses machine learning to automatically discover, classify, and protect sensitive data, including personally identifiable information (PII). By configuring Amazon Macie in each region where the company stores PII data, you can create jobs to analyze the data in Amazon S3 and identify any PII.

q: A company runs applications on AWS that connect to the company's Amazon RDS database. The applications scale on weekends and at peak times of the year. The company wants to scale the database more effectively for its applications that connect to the database. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.t: Use Amazon RDS Proxy with a target group for the database. Change the applications to use the RDS Proxy endpoint.
o.w: An EC2 instance with a GP3 EBS volume closely replicates locally-attached block storage behavior with no application changes required, and GP3 lets you provision IOPS and throughput independently of volume size at a lower baseline cost than GP2, making it the most cost-effective lift-and-shift option.

o.t: Use Amazon DynamoDB with connection pooling with a target group configuration for the database. Change the applications to use the DynamoDB endpoint.
o.w: FSx for Lustre is a high-performance shared file system designed for HPC and large-scale parallel workloads; it is unrelated to migrating a simple locally-attached-storage application without changing its architecture, and it adds unnecessary cost and complexity here.

o.t: Use an AWS Lambda function to provide connection pooling with a target group configuration for the database. Change the applications to use the Lambda function.
o.w: GP2 volumes tie IOPS to volume size and generally cost more per unit of performance than GP3 for an equivalent performance level, making GP3 the more cost-effective choice for this lift-and-shift.

o.t: Use a custom proxy that runs on Amazon EC2 as an intermediary to the database. Change the applications to use the custom proxy endpoint.
o.w: FSx for OpenZFS is a managed shared network file system, a different storage paradigm than simple locally-attached block storage, requiring more architectural change than a straightforward lift and shift calls for.

q: A company is implementing new data retention policies for all databases that run on Amazon RDS DB instances. The company must retain daily backups for a minimum period of 2 years. The backups must be consistent and restorable. Which solution should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

o.t: Configure database transaction logs to be automatically backed up to Amazon CloudWatch Logs with an expiration period of 2 years.
o.w: Direct Connect gateways are intended for connecting on-premises networks over Direct Connect to multiple VPCs and Regions; they are not the standard least-effort mechanism for general VPC-to-VPC mesh connectivity across many VPCs and Regions.

o.t: Create a backup vault in AWS Backup to retain RDS backups. Create a new backup plan with a daily schedule and an expiration period of 2 years after creation. Assign the RDS DB instances to the backup plan.
o.w: AWS PrivateLink is designed for exposing a specific service endpoint privately between VPCs (one-to-many service access), not for general full-mesh network connectivity among many VPCs across multiple Regions.

o.t: Configure an AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) replication task. Deploy a replication instance, and configure a change data capture (CDC) task to stream database changes to Amazon S3 as the target. Configure S3 Lifecycle policies to delete the snapshots after 2 years.
o.w: VPC peering connections are not transitive, so connecting every VPC to every other VPC would require configuring and managing a large number of individual point-to-point peering connections — an operationally heavy full mesh, especially across multiple Regions.

o.t: Configure a backup window for the RDS DB instances for daily snapshots. Assign a snapshot retention policy of 2 years to each RDS DB instance. Use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (Amazon DLM) to schedule snapshot deletions.
o.w: AWS Transit Gateway provides hub-and-spoke connectivity for many VPCs within a Region, and Transit Gateway peering extends that connectivity across Regions, letting the company manage all inter-VPC communication through a small number of centralized gateways with the least administrative effort.

q: A company has deployed a web application on AWS. The company hosts the backend database on Amazon RDS for MySQL with a primary DB instance and five read replicas to support scaling needs. The read replicas must lag no more than 1 second behind the primary DB instance. The database routinely runs scheduled stored procedures. As traffic on the website increases, the replicas experience additional lag during periods of peak load. A solutions architect must reduce the replication lag as much as possible. The solutions architect must minimize changes to the application code and must minimize ongoing operational overhead. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.t: Migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB. Provision a large number of read capacity units (RCUs) to support the required throughput, and configure on-demand capacity scaling. Replace the stored procedures with DynamoDB streams.
o.w: Amazon Inspector is a vulnerability assessment service for EC2, container, and Lambda security posture; it does not inspect or block live HTTP requests for SQL injection patterns.

o.t: Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora MySQL. Replace the read replicas with Aurora Replicas, and configure Aurora Auto Scaling. Replace the stored procedures with Aurora MySQL native functions.
o.w: AWS Shield Advanced protects against DDoS attacks; it is not designed to detect or block application-layer attacks such as SQL injection.

o.t: Migrate the database to a MySQL database that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. Choose large, compute optimized EC2 instances for all replica nodes. Maintain the stored procedures on the EC2 instances.
o.w: AWS WAF, placed in front of the ALB with appropriate web ACL rules (including managed SQL injection rule sets), inspects and blocks malicious HTTP requests like SQL injection attempts before they reach the application, directly addressing the vulnerability.

o.t: Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster in front of the database. Modify the application to check the cache before the application queries the database. Replace the stored procedures with AWS Lambda functions.
o.w: An ALB listener rule that returns a fixed response doesn't actually detect or filter SQL injection payloads; it only applies a static response under specific routing conditions and is not a security inspection mechanism.

explain:
Amazon Aurora MySQL: Aurora Replicas in Amazon Aurora MySQL are designed to have minimal replication lag compared to traditional MySQL read replicas. Aurora is built for high performance and low replication lag, making it a suitable choice for reducing lag in read replicas.

Aurora Auto Scaling: Aurora Auto Scaling allows you to automatically adjust the number of Aurora Replicas based on actual application usage. This ensures that you have the right amount of read capacity during periods of peak load, minimizing replication lag.

q: A global company runs its applications in multiple AWS accounts in AWS Organizations. The company's applications use multipart uploads to upload data to multiple Amazon S3 buckets across AWS Regions. The company wants to report on incomplete multipart uploads for cost compliance purposes. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.t: Configure S3 Storage Lens to report the incomplete multipart upload object count.
o.w: Taking periodic EC2 snapshots and sending them to another Region addresses backup and disaster recovery, not the real-time high availability of the currently running application.

o.t: Create a service control policy (SCP) to report the incomplete multipart upload object count.
o.w: Deploying the stateless application across multiple Availability Zones with an Auto Scaling group and an Application Load Balancer removes the single-AZ point of failure and distributes traffic across healthy instances in multiple AZs, directly achieving high availability.

o.t: Create an S3 Multi-Region Access Point to report the incomplete multipart upload object count.
o.w: A 'Multi-AZ Application Load Balancer' configured through Route 53 rules isn't a meaningful distinct concept — an ALB already spans multiple AZs once subnets in multiple AZs are selected, so this option doesn't actually move the EC2 tier out of its single Availability Zone.

o.t: Configure AWS Config with a rule to report the incomplete multipart upload object count.
o.w: Route 53 latency-based routing is used to route users to the closest of multiple separate regional deployments; it does not solve the immediate problem that the EC2 tier is confined to a single Availability Zone.

explain:
S3 Storage Lens is a feature in Amazon S3 that provides a comprehensive view of your storage usage and activity across multiple accounts. It helps you understand, analyze, and optimize your storage usage.
You can use S3 Storage Lens to generate reports on various metrics, including the incomplete multipart upload object count.

q: A solutions architect is designing a new API using Amazon API Gateway that will receive requests from users. The volume of requests is highly variable; several hours can pass without receiving a single request. The data processing will take place asynchronously, but should be completed within a few seconds after a request is made. Which compute service should the solutions architect have the API invoke to deliver the requirements at the lowest cost?

o.t: An AWS Lambda function
o.w: A Provisioned IOPS EBS volume can generally only be attached to one instance at a time for active read/write without specialized Multi-Attach clustering, so it isn't naturally suited to being modified concurrently by multiple instances across Availability Zones.

o.t: A containerized service hosted in Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
o.w: A standard EBS volume is tied to a single Availability Zone and cannot be mounted by instances in other AZs, so it doesn't meet the requirement for data modified by instances deployed across multiple Availability Zones.

o.t: A containerized service hosted in Amazon ECS with Amazon EC2
o.w: Amazon EFS is a fully managed, elastic file system that can be mounted concurrently by multiple EC2 instances across Availability Zones, and it automatically scales storage capacity as the dataset grows, fitting the growing, shared, hourly-analyzed dataset.

o.t: An AWS Glue job
o.w: Amazon S3 Glacier is designed for infrequently accessed archival data, not for data that needs to be actively modified hourly by multiple EC2 instances, and it is not a mountable, directly writable filesystem.

explain: AWS Lambda supports asynchronous invocation, which is suitable for scenarios where data processing can take place independently of the API request and complete within a few seconds. This aligns with the requirement of processing data asynchronously.

q: An online retail company has more than 50 million active customers and receives more than 25,000 orders each day. The company collects purchase data for customers and stores this data in Amazon S3. Additional customer data is stored in Amazon RDS. The company wants to make all the data available to various teams so that the teams can perform analytics. The solution must provide the ability to manage fine-grained permissions for the data and must minimize operational overhead. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.t: Schedule an AWS Lambda function to periodically copy data from Amazon RDS to Amazon S3. Create an AWS Glue crawler. Use Amazon Athena to query the data. Use S3 policies to limit access.
o.w: Loading all the data into ElastiCache requires significant changes to the application and query logic to work against a cache instead of SQL, which is more than the minimal change the requirement calls for.

o.t: Create a data lake by using AWS Lake Formation. Create an AWS Glue JDBC connection to Amazon RDS. Register the S3 bucket in Lake Formation. Use Lake Formation access controls to limit access.
o.w: Copying data into a separate Redshift cluster is a bigger architectural shift (ETL pipeline, different query engine) than necessary just to offload simple read-only SQL queries with minimal application change.

o.t: Create an Amazon Redshift cluster. Schedule an AWS Lambda function to periodically copy data from Amazon S3 and Amazon RDS to Amazon Redshift. Use Amazon Redshift access controls to limit access.
o.w: Creating an RDS read replica lets business analysts' read-only queries run against the replica instead of the primary, requiring only a connection-endpoint change for the reporting users and minimal changes to the existing web application.

o.t: Migrate the purchase data to write directly to Amazon RDS. Use RDS access controls to limit access.
o.w: Exporting all the data into DynamoDB would require rewriting the analysts' SQL queries into a NoSQL access pattern, which is a far bigger change than the minimal modification the requirement specifies.

explain:
AWS Lake Formation is designed to create a secure and scalable data lake in Amazon S3. By creating a data lake with Lake Formation, you can centrally manage access controls, fine-grained permissions, and define granular data access policies. This simplifies the process of granting and managing permissions for various teams.

In this scenario, you can use AWS Glue to create a JDBC connection to Amazon RDS for accessing the additional customer data. The S3 bucket, where the purchase data is stored, can be registered in Lake Formation. Lake Formation allows you to set up fine-grained access controls and permissions, providing the ability to manage who can access specific data within the data lake.

q: A media company collects and analyzes user activity data on premises. The company wants to migrate this capability to AWS. The user activity data store will continue to grow and will be petabytes in size. The company needs to build a highly available data ingestion solution that facilitates on-demand analytics of existing data and new data with SQL. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

o.t: Send activity data to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Configure the stream to deliver the data to an Amazon S3 bucket.
o.w: ACM-issued certificates and enabling SSL/TLS protect data in transit by encrypting the connection; they do nothing to encrypt the data stored at rest in the database.

o.t: Send activity data to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream. Configure the stream to deliver the data to an Amazon Redshift cluster.
o.w: IAM does not issue SSL/TLS certificates, and in any case an SSL/TLS certificate encrypts data in transit, not the data stored at rest in the database.

o.t: Create an ingestion service on Amazon EC2 instances that are spread across multiple Availability Zones. Configure the service to forward data to an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ database.
o.w: Creating a key in AWS KMS and enabling encryption on the RDS DB instance directly satisfies the requirement to encrypt data at rest, since RDS integrates natively with KMS for storage-level encryption.

o.t: Place activity data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure Amazon S3 to run an AWS Lambda function on the data as the data arrives in the S3 bucket.
o.w: AWS Secrets Manager is designed to store and rotate secrets like database credentials, not to serve as the encryption key management service for RDS storage encryption — that role belongs to AWS KMS, not Secrets Manager.

explain:
Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose: It is a fully managed service that simplifies the delivery of streaming data to destinations such as Amazon S3, Amazon Redshift, or Amazon Elasticsearch Service. It handles the scaling, buffering, and delivery of data.

Amazon Redshift: It is a fully managed, petabyte-scale data warehouse service. It is optimized for high-performance analysis using standard SQL queries.

Least Operational Overhead: Kinesis Data Firehose takes care of many operational aspects, including scaling and buffering, reducing the operational overhead on your part. Configuring it to deliver data to Amazon Redshift provides a streamlined and managed solution.

q: A company runs an application that receives data from thousands of geographically dispersed remote devices that use UDP. The application processes the data immediately and sends a message back to the device if necessary. No data is stored. The company needs a solution that minimizes latency for the data transmission from the devices. The solution also must provide rapid failover to another AWS Region. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.t: Configure an Amazon Route 53 failover routing policy. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in each of the two Regions. Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with the Fargate launch type. Create an ECS service on the cluster. Set the ECS service as the target for the ALB. Process the data in Amazon ECS.
o.w: Simply cloning the instance and load-balancing connections distributes incoming requests but doesn't decouple job submission from processing capacity or scale based on actual backlog, so instances can still remain saturated at 100% CPU under heavy load.

o.t: Use AWS Global Accelerator. Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in each of the two Regions as an endpoint. Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with the Fargate launch type. Create an ECS service on the cluster. Set the ECS service as the target for the NLProcess the data in Amazon ECS.
o.w: Moving to a larger single instance type raises the processing ceiling but doesn't provide elastic, demand-based scaling, and a single instance can still become a bottleneck during unpredictable spikes in job volume.

o.t: Configure an Amazon Route 53 failover routing policy. Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in each of the two Regions. Configure the NLB to invoke an AWS Lambda function to process the data.
o.w: An S3 VPC endpoint improves the network path and cost for accessing S3, but it does not address the compute-bound processing bottleneck or enable scaling based on job load.

o.t: Use AWS Global Accelerator. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in each of the two Regions as an endpoint. Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster with the Fargate launch type. Create an ECS service on the cluster. Set the ECS service as the target for the ALB. Process the data in Amazon ECS.
o.w: Routing job requests into an SQS queue decouples ingestion from processing, and configuring EC2 Auto Scaling based on queue depth lets the fleet scale out and in to match actual processing demand, resolving dropped jobs and the sustained 100% CPU utilization.

explain:
AWS Global Accelerator: AWS Global Accelerator provides static IP addresses that act as a fixed entry point to your application. It routes traffic over the AWS global network to the optimal AWS endpoint based on health, geography, and routing policies.

Network Load Balancer (NLB): NLB is well-suited for UDP-based traffic, and it's designed for high-performance, low-latency applications. In this case, it can efficiently handle the thousands of geographically dispersed remote devices sending UDP traffic.

Amazon ECS with Fargate Launch Type: Using ECS with Fargate allows you to deploy and run containers without managing the underlying infrastructure. This setup can efficiently handle the immediate processing of data without the need to manage the underlying servers.

q: A company has an on-premises server that uses an Oracle database to process and store customer information. The company wants to use an AWS database service to achieve higher availability and to improve application performance. The company also wants to offload reporting from its primary database system. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

o.t: Use Amazon RDS deployed in a Multi-AZ instance deployment to create an Amazon Aurora database. Direct the reporting functions to the reader instances.
o.w: Scratch file systems are designed for temporary, short-term high-performance processing and are not replicated for durability or high availability, so they don't meet the requirement for a highly available, durable storage solution.

o.t: Use Amazon RDS in a Single-AZ deployment to create an Oracle database. Create a read replica in the same zone as the primary DB instance. Direct the reporting functions to the read replica.
o.w: EFS Bursting Throughput mode scales throughput with the amount of data stored and relies on burst credits, so it cannot reliably provide the sustained, extremely high, sub-millisecond-latency throughput that thousands of simultaneously-accessing HPC compute instances require.

o.t: Use Amazon RDS deployed in a Multi-AZ cluster deployment to create an Oracle database. Direct the reporting functions to use the reader instance in the cluster deployment.
o.w: EFS Provisioned Throughput mode allows setting a fixed throughput level independent of storage size, but EFS as an NFS-based service generally cannot match the sub-millisecond latency and extreme sustained throughput that a purpose-built HPC parallel file system delivers.

o.t: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to create an Amazon RDS DB instance in multiple AWS Regions. Point the reporting functions toward a separate DB instance from the primary DB instance.
o.w: FSx for Lustre persistent file systems are designed for longer-term, highly available, durable storage that can sustain very high throughput and low latency across thousands of simultaneously-accessing compute instances, directly matching the HPC requirements.

explain: Deploying Amazon RDS in a Multi-AZ instance deployment ensures high availability by replicating the primary database instance in a different Availability Zone (AZ). This provides automatic failover in case of a hardware failure or maintenance event.

q: A company is building a new furniture inventory application. The company has deployed the application on a fleet ofAmazon EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones. The EC2 instances run behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in their VPC. A solutions architect has observed that incoming traffic seems to favor one EC2 instance, resulting in latency for some requests. What should the solutions architect do to resolve this issue?

o.t: Increase the number of EC2 instances in each Availability Zone
o.w: AWS Transfer Family provides a fully managed SFTP endpoint for Amazon S3 and supports integrating with on-premises Active Directory for authentication, letting the customer's existing SFTP client and AD credentials work unchanged with no custom infrastructure to manage.

o.t: Replace the ALB with a Network Load Balancer
o.w: AWS DMS is designed for database migration and replication, not for providing an SFTP file-transfer interface to S3, so it would not support the customer's existing SFTP client workflow at all.

o.t: Adjust the frequency of the health checks on the ALB's target group
o.w: AWS DataSync is built for data transfer and synchronization using its own agents and protocols, not an SFTP interface, and pairing it with IAM Identity Center still doesn't give the customer's SFTP client unchanged access to S3.

o.t: Disable session affinity (sticky sessions) on the ALB
o.w: Standing up and maintaining a Windows EC2 instance running SFTP software requires the company to patch, scale, and manage that server itself, which is far more operational overhead than using the fully managed Transfer Family service.

explain: Session affinity, also known as sticky sessions, directs a client's requests to the same EC2 instance, based on the client's session information. While sticky sessions can be useful in some scenarios, they can lead to uneven distribution of traffic, causing latency for some requests if one EC2 instance is overloaded.

q: A company is building an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster for its workloads. All secrets that are stored in Amazon EKS must be encrypted in the Kubernetes etcd key-value store. Which solution will meet these requirements?

o.t: Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key with the alias/aws/ebs alias. Enable default Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume encryption for the account.
o.w: AWS Fargate for the backend adds container management and per-task pricing that is generally costlier than Spot EC2 pricing for simple variable-workload nodes, introducing a different operating model without a clear cost benefit for this use case.

o.t: Create the Amazon EKS cluster with default options. Use the Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Container Storage Interface (CSI) driver as an add-on.
o.w: Using Spot Instances for the frontend nodes that must run 24/7 risks interruption of a workload that needs constant uptime, which is the wrong trade-off — availability would be compromised for savings that are better captured elsewhere.

o.t: Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key. Enable Amazon EKS KMS secrets encryption on the Amazon EKS cluster.
o.w: Spot Instances for the always-on frontend still risk interruptions to a workload that needs continuous uptime, undermining 24/7 availability even though Fargate could reasonably handle the variable backend.

o.t: Create a new AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key. Use AWS Secrets Manager to manage, rotate, and store all secrets in Amazon EKS.
o.w: Reserved Instances commit to a discount for the frontend nodes that run continuously 24/7, while Spot Instances take advantage of cheap, interruptible capacity for the flexible, scale-out/scale-in backend nodes — matching each pricing model to the workload pattern that best fits it for maximum cost savings.
